recognize_zh: 周邊血片中央有一顆比嗜中性球大很多的細胞，細胞核不規則折疊、染色質較粗，灰藍色細胞質豐富且充滿大小不一的空泡，細胞邊緣呈不規則突起，這樣的形態符合循環中的組織球（histiocyte）。
features: Large cell, roughly two to three times the diameter of adjacent neutrophils
Irregular, folded to reniform eccentric nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin
Abundant grey-blue cytoplasm with numerous small vacuoles and fine granules
No definite phagocytosed cells or organisms visible
Background with neutrophils, numerous platelets, and unremarkable red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large mononuclear cell with an irregular, folded eccentric nucleus and abundant grey-blue, extensively vacuolated cytoplasm with irregular borders. No ingested red cells, leukocytes, or organisms are identified within this cell. Adjacent neutrophils and platelets appear unremarkable. Findings are consistent with a circulating histiocyte/macrophage, which can be seen in severe infection, hemophagocytic states, or after intravascular stress, and should prompt review for intracellular organisms or phagocytosed cells.

ddx.vs: Monocytes are smaller with fine lacy chromatin and grey cytoplasm with fewer vacuoles, whereas histiocytes are larger with more abundant cytoplasm and frayed borders; distinction is often imprecise on blood smears.
Blasts have fine open chromatin with nucleoli, and are typically numerous rather than a single isolated mature-appearing cell.

ddx.dx: Endothelial cell or other circulating non-hematopoietic cell
ddx.vs: Endothelial cells are elongated with oval nuclei and scant non-vacuolated cytoplasm and often appear in clusters.
